name: Finish the Line Karaoke
why_it_works: An unfinished pattern is almost painful to leave. Lyrics on screen with a bouncing highlight let viewers sing along, then the last word drops out and their brain sings it for them. That small win drives replays and duets.

hook.pattern: Show the karaoke lyric bar and dare the viewer to finish the last word before it appears.
examples: Sing the last word. Bet you already know it.
Nobody gets the last line right on the first try.
Duet this if you can finish the line.

variables.name: song_title
variables.description: Original song title (the missing last word)

variables.name: line_one
variables.example: You pull me in like the tide pulls the moon

variables.name: line_two
variables.description: Second lyric line, ends one word before the title
variables.example: Every time I fall I blame it on the

variables.name: listen_link
variables.description: Where to hear or buy it

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 portrait of {{artist_name}} holding a mic toward the camera like offering it to the viewer, moody purple and teal stage light, shallow depth of field

beats.purpose: karaoke line one with bouncing highlight
line two stops before the title word
silent gap for viewer to sing
reveal title word plus where to hear it

visual.prompt: Vertical slow push-in on {{artist_name}} singing the final word with eyes closed, lights blooming on the downbeat, haze, 9:16

cta: Duet this and finish the line. Full song '{{song_title}}': {{listen_link}}.

slides.headline: Finish the line
slides.visual_prompt: Bold title slide, {{artist_name}} name in big type, karaoke-style lyric bar graphic, dark background with neon accent

slides.headline: Line one
slides.visual_prompt: Lyric slide, white words on black, first word highlighted in neon like a karaoke bounce

slides.headline: Line two

slides.headline: Say it out loud

slides.headline: {{song_title}}
slides.body: That's the one. Now hear the whole thing.
slides.visual_prompt: Cover-art style slide with {{song_title}} in large type over a portrait of {{artist_name}}

slides.headline: Hear it now

craft.notes: Title placement: the title is the last word of the couplet and the rhyme partner of line one, so the ear predicts it. Line one ends on a stressed vowel sound the title echoes (moon / gravity works via internal assonance; a hard end-rhyme works even better). Stress the final syllable before the title on beat 4 so the title lands on the next beat 1, then cut the audio for exactly one beat. Tempo/feel: 76-84 BPM, half-time pop or R&B, sparse keys and a deep kick so the silence feels intentional.

do_not: Use someone else's lyrics, even a famous line people would know
Make the missing word guessable only if you already know the song
Let the highlight run ahead of the vocal; viewers lose the sing-along
